sections.html:
Lauderhill incorporated on June 20, 1959 with about 100 residents. It now covers 8.5 square miles in Broward County, has a population of 74,479 and uses zip codes 33311, 33313, 33319 and 33351. Homes range from single-family houses to multi-family buildings and townhouses.

  • State whether the house is single-family, a townhouse or part of an association.
  • Confirm school assignment with the district before naming a school in a listing.
  • Mention the city's Community Bus Shuttle if your address is near a route.

sections.h2: Who signs the deed when the owner has died?
sections.html:
First settle who has legal authority to sign. If the owner died holding the house alone, a court usually has to name a personal representative before a title company will close.

Florida allows summary administration for smaller estates, when countable assets stay at or under $150,000, and also once two years have gone by since death (s. 735.201). A house still counts as real property, so Lauderhill heirs normally need some court step. Creditors get a limited window: the later of three months from first publication of the notice to creditors or 30 days from service on a known creditor (s. 733.702).

  • Gather the death certificate, the will if there is one, and the deed.
  • Ask the Broward clerk what the probate division requires for a house.
  • Pay taxes and insurance on time until the estate closes.

sections.h2: Estate tax and deed tax on an inherited house
sections.html:
No state estate tax applies. Florida's ended for deaths after December 31, 2004, and filing Form DR-312 or DR-313 has been unnecessary since July 1, 2023.

Heirs sometimes expect closing costs to look like an ordinary sale. They vary with the type of deed and the people who sign it. Ask the closing agent for a line-by-line estimate before the estate accepts any price, and keep that estimate with the estate records.

A personal representative's deed under a probated will is on the state's not-taxable list for documentary stamps. An ordinary sale deed is not: it carries the stamp rate in s. 201.02, seventy cents for every hundred dollars of price in Broward, and the signers share liability.

sections.h2: Homestead and the tax cap after a death or sale
sections.html:
Both reset. Homestead depends on the owner living in the house as a permanent residence on January 1, and renting it out or moving away ends it.

Under Save Our Homes, yearly growth in assessed value stops at 3 percent or CPI, whichever is smaller, and the state's chart printed 2.7 percent for 2026. After a sale or other change of title, the following January 1 brings a fresh valuation at just value (s. 193.155). Heirs who keep and rent the house should expect a higher bill than the decedent's.

sections.h2: Tax dates for a Lauderhill seller
sections.html:
The county property appraiser sets values and approves exemptions, and the tax collector bills.

Property tax steps for a Broward County home
StepTimingOffice
File for exemptionsBy March 1Property appraiser
Proposed tax notice (TRIM)AugustProperty appraiser
Challenge a valueWithin 25 days of the noticeClerk of the court
Tax billsNovemberTax collector
DelinquencyApril 1Tax collector

An unpaid bill on an inherited parcel deserves a call to the tax collector for the exact amount, because the clock toward a June 1 certificate sale keeps moving.

sections.h2: City permits, code cases and liens
sections.html:
For permits, code questions or a certificate of occupancy, call the city before pricing. Unpermitted work that a buyer discovers can slow a closing. The city's neighborhood district meetings also show what neighbors are asking it to fix, which is useful background before you set a price.

  • Ask whether open permits or code cases exist on the address.
  • Have the title company search for municipal liens.
  • Keep receipts for repairs you complete before selling.

sections.h2: Comparing offers on an inherited house
sections.html:
Put every offer on one sheet with the same lines: price, repairs the buyer expects you to make, who pays the deed tax, who pays recording, and the closing date. An offer that looks high can lose that lead once those lines are filled in.

Ask whether the buyer closes with no financing contingency, whether a deposit becomes non-refundable, and what happens if the estate needs extra weeks for court paperwork. A cash purchase tends to suit a house the heirs do not want to repair, with belongings inside and family out of state. A listing may bring a higher price when the house is clean and the estate can wait.

Photograph each room before anything leaves, and decide in writing who gets which keepsakes. Disagreements among heirs can stall a closing as surely as a missing document. Name one heir to speak with buyers and the title company, so every question gets a single answer.

sections.h2: Clearing and preparing an inherited house
sections.html:
Set aside a weekend or two. Walk through with a list and sort contents into keep, donate, sell and discard piles. Keep personal papers, tax returns, insurance policies and anything with an account number in a locked box until the estate attorney says what to retain.

Check that utilities stay on, the locks are changed, and the insurer knows the owner has died, since a vacant house can change coverage terms. Mow, remove mail and flyers, and photograph the condition so you can show what the buyer saw.

If the house needs work and no heir wants to manage contractors, an as-is sale shifts that job to the buyer. Get the price in writing and compare it to what a repaired house might bring after months of effort and carrying costs.

sections.h2: How an estate sale moves, step by step
sections.html:
Begin with the court. The personal representative gets letters of administration, then the title company reviews them along with the death certificate and the deed. With those in hand the representative can sign a contract, and a buyer can start a title search.

Meanwhile, ask the tax collector for the exact balance on the parcel and ask the insurer to keep the policy active. At closing the representative signs the deed before two witnesses, the clerk records it, and the proceeds go to the estate, not to any single heir. The estate attorney then guides how the money is split.

Heirs who live far away should send ID copies and signed forms early. A missing signature from one relative is a frequent cause of delay.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell before the estate closes?
faqs.a: Usually not until a personal representative has authority to convey. A probate attorney or the Broward clerk can say whether summary administration fits, which turns on the $150,000 threshold or two years since death. Bring the death certificate and deed to that first conversation.

faqs.q: Does Florida charge estate tax on a house passed to heirs?
faqs.a: No. The state tax ended for deaths after December 31, 2004.

faqs.q: What is the Save Our Homes cap in 2026?
faqs.a: The state chart printed 2.7 percent for 2026. The smaller of 3 percent or CPI sets it, and a sale starts the clock over.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax when a Lauderhill house sells?
faqs.a: The signers share liability whichever party the contract names, at seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price in Broward (s. 201.02).
Ask the school district. Confirm the assignment before you name a school in a listing.
